purpose: Diagnostic comparison of no update, one predefined small displacement along the actual last applied update, and the full update; no parameter selection by score.
checkpoint: Immediately after the 24th training outcome and its weight update, before the 25th note.
update_vector: For each selected edge, d = recorded post-update weight minus its pre-update weight; zero for an unchanged edge.
small_rule: epsilon=min(1,0.004 mV/max_abs(d)); the largest small displacement is at most 10% of the initial 0.04 mV edge weight.
primary_probe: Original saved 16 frozen notes with plasticity and exploration disabled, preserving map times and cue gains.
secondary_probe: Same 16 notes with plasticity disabled and the original exploration process enabled. Three streams: inherited checkpoint RNG state and future states generated from seed XOR 324508639 and seed XOR 610839776; the identical stream is used in every weight branch.
metrics: mean original per-note utility and judgement distribution
signed and absolute hit error, conditioned on scored non-MISS presses
all DOWN times and dispositions, including null presses
initial lower/upper weight-bound occupancy and raw/applied last-update norms
decision_rules: If the small update improves paired utility while the full update reduces it on the same probes, support oversized-step or clipping, not a universal conclusion.
If both small and full changes move timing away from zero and lower paired utility, support a locally unfavorable update direction.
If utility is tied at existing judgement tiers, report directional timing evidence and leave the reward-gradient question unresolved.
If effects depend on exploration mode or stream, report a policy mismatch or instability rather than a robust improvement.
selection_limit: These three cases were chosen from known outcomes in the previous diagnosis. They estimate mechanisms, not prevalence or a confirmatory reliability rate.
